The energy gradient theory can reveal the physical mechanism of flow instability in a differentially heated cavity.
The fin length has a negligible effect on heat transfer when the Rayleigh number is relatively high.
The most efficient heat transfer rate is achieved when the fin is fixed at the middle height of the cavity.
The fin blocks heat transfer when the Rayleigh number is relatively small.
The fin enhances heat transfer when the Rayleigh number is relatively large.
A linear correlation is obtained between the energy gradient function and Rayleigh number.
The Prandtl number of water is 6.67.
The Prandtl number of air is 0.67.
The Rayleigh number range studied in this paper is from 10^4 to 10^9.
The aspect ratio of the cavity studied in this paper is 0.24.
The numerical algorithm used in this paper is finite-volume SIMPLE scheme with the QUICK scheme approximating the advection term.
The grid independence test used in this paper involves four different grid systems with mesh sizes of 0.004, 0.003, 0.002, and 0.0015.
The energy gradient function is a dimensionless field variable that expresses the ratio of the energy gained in a half-period by the particle and the energy loss due to viscosity in the half-period.
The criterion of stability in the energy gradient theory is the ratio of the energy gained in a half-period by the particle and the energy loss due to viscosity in the half-period.
The energy gradient theory can be used to explain the physical mechanism of flow instability in natural convection.
The study of flow instability in a differentially heated cavity is important for understanding heat transfer and fluid dynamics.
The energy gradient theory provides a new perspective on the physical mechanism of flow instability in natural convection.
